paragraphs.text: Which was in the king's house at Jerusalem, as in Jer 32:1,2.
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: That is, of Jerusalem, who as he made it, so will he preserve it, read Isa 37:26.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: The Jews think to overcome the Chaldeans, but they seek their own destruction.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: He shows that God's favour is cause of all prosperity, as his anger is of all adversity.
paragraphs.label: e

paragraphs.text: In the midst of his threatenings God remembers his, and comforts them.
paragraphs.label: f
paragraphs.anchor: will bring it health and cure

paragraphs.text: Declaring that there is no deliverance nor joy, but where we feel remission of sins.
paragraphs.label: g
paragraphs.anchor: cleanse them from all their iniquity

paragraphs.text: By which he shows that the Church in which is remission of sins, is God's honour and glory, so that whoever is enemy to it, labours to dishonour God.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: Which was a song appointed for the Levites to praise God by, 1Ch 16:8; Ps 105:1; 106:1; 107:1; 118:1; 136:1; Isa 12:4
paragraphs.label: i

paragraphs.text: Meaning that all the country of Judah will be inhabited again.
paragraphs.label: k

paragraphs.text: That is, I will send the Messiah, who will come of the house of David, of whom this prophecy is meant, as testify all the Jews and that which is written, Jer 23:5.
paragraphs.label: l
paragraphs.anchor: the Branch of righteousness to grow

paragraphs.text: That is, Christ that will call his Church.
paragraphs.label: m

paragraphs.text: That is, Christ is our Lord God, our righteousness, sanctification and redemption, 1Co 1:30.
paragraphs.label: n

paragraphs.text: That is, chiefly meant of the spiritual sacrifice of thanksgiving which is left to the Church in the time of Christ, who was the everlasting priest and the everlasting sacrifice figured by the sacrifices of the law.
paragraphs.label: o

paragraphs.text: Meaning, the Chaldeans and other infidels who thought God had utterly cast off Judah and Israel or Benjamin, because he corrected them for a time for their amendment.
paragraphs.label: q
